records.name: Gradual Blur
records.summary: Gradual Blur is a public React Bits animation with four official React variants: JavaScript or TypeScript, each with CSS or Tailwind.
records.technique: Open the official live demo, choose the TypeScript/JavaScript and CSS/Tailwind variant that matches the project, then install only that registry item and adapt its props.
records.style_tags: animated; React; React Bits; Animation; gradual; blur
records.best_for: hero accents; interactive details; expressive transitions; portfolio moments
records.dependencies: Dependencies vary by component; inspect the official page and registry payload before installation.
records.framework_fit: React; official JavaScript/TypeScript and CSS/Tailwind variants
records.motion_choreography: Preserve the core interaction idea, retime it to the brand, pause it offscreen, and remove continuous motion when it no longer supports attention.
records.accessibility_contract: Preserve semantic HTML beneath the effect, keyboard and touch parity, visible focus, sufficient contrast, and a meaningful prefers-reduced-motion state.
records.content_contract: Replace every demo asset and string with real project content. The visual effect must never obscure essential information or controls.
records.responsive_strategy: Reduce effect density, pointer dependence, resolution, and continuous animation on narrow screens and coarse-pointer devices; retain the underlying content.
records.interaction_inputs: Inspect the official demo for pointer, scroll, drag, keyboard, and ambient inputs before integration.
records.fallback_strategy: Keep an equivalent static or plain-HTML state when motion, canvas, WebGL, pointer precision, or runtime dependencies are unavailable.
records.test_focus: official dependency check; reduced motion; keyboard and touch parity; narrow viewport; offscreen pause; cleanup; loading; canvas/WebGL fallback
records.implementation_steps: open official source; choose the correct framework variant; install only the selected component; audit dependencies; brand-adapt; add fallback; profile and test
records.brand_tokens: Map exposed colors, type, radii, spacing, imagery, lighting, and motion values to the project's semantic tokens.
records.avoid_when: the effect competes with the page goal, duplicates another signature moment, weakens readability, or cannot provide an accessible fallback
records.usage_rights: Use and adapt in personal or commercial applications, websites, and products.
records.resale_restriction: Do not sell, sublicense, or redistribute the components themselves, alone, bundled, or ported.
records.creator: David Haz
records.pairing_guidance: Use this wherever it improves hierarchy, feedback, storytelling, comprehension, or brand character. It may be combined with other compatible records; avoid duplication because it weakens the design, not because of a catalog limit.
records.codex_selection_instruction: Available discovery source: React Bits. Use any compatible ideas from this record that improve the design, combine them with other records when useful, or omit them. The catalog does not limit the number of selected components.
records.enhancement_slot_policy: No fixed component or enhancement quota. Start with a coherent set, then add every additional treatment that has a clear purpose and remains visually compatible.
records.stacking_limit: Advisory runtime budget, not a count limit. Multiple lightweight effects and multiple section backgrounds are allowed; lazy-load and pause heavy scenes so only the relevant work stays active, and test the combined result.
records.selection_freedom: Advisory library, not a quota system. Codex may use, combine, adapt, repeat, or omit any number of records from any source when they fit the page goal and art direction.
records.runtime_budget_guidance: Judge simultaneous cost rather than total selections. Multiple heavy scenes may exist on one page when separated by section, lazy-loaded, paused offscreen, given static fallbacks, and verified on target devices.
